correctness.rationale: The face criterion is proved equivalent to induced component size at most two. Exact enumeration visits all 4095 nonempty masks, giving 521 faces. The embedded 243-pair matching certificate covers 486 distinct faces; all 1800 nonempty face-poset covering edges are checked and the directed graph is acyclic by a complete 521-vertex topological sort. Only one critical vertex and 34 critical 3-faces remain; discrete Morse theory therefore proves the integral wedge of 34 three-spheres. A separate forbidden-triple enumerator reproduces the face set and GF(2) boundary ranks; exact signed fixed-simplex sums for all 24 dihedral symmetries produce the character. Graph-intrinsic common-neighbor counts establish the full group as D12. Finite exhaustive proof is not extrapolated to any other graph.

originality.rationale: Actual records and source comparisons reveal no exact, equivalent or stronger coverage. The complete multipartite PF3 result does not imply this nonmultipartite example; general tree and chordal graph theorems do not apply to a graph containing an induced six-cycle. The scientific novelty is the exact integral homotopy class jointly with the full dihedral representation, not a claim of unique discovery.

value.rationale: The hexagonal antiprism is a canonical 12-vertex vertex-transitive planar polyhedral graph, a distinguished case of cycle-square circulants. The exact integral homotopy type of its first higher-independence complex is a nonroutine natural invariant: a nonpure complex extending through dimension five contracts in Morse theory to 34 independent three-sphere cells. The complete 24-element dihedral homology character detects four globally invariant directions and a 22/12 antipodal split, data not derivable from Euler characteristics or the known tree/multipartite results. These computations make a substantive reproducible finite benchmark for the topological behavior of three-path-free complexes on a natural cyclic-square family; no general family theorem is claimed.
